solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Exotic satin dress strap Pole might display

definitions.note: a Pole here is a flagpole, and the flag it flies is the definition

indicators.note: exotic suggests something strange and unfamiliar, so the following letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An outlandish satin dress strap worn by someone from Poland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' looks like a person from Poland, but it is a flagpole; 'Exotic' rearranges SATIN DRESS STRAP.
explanation.definitionFit: The flag of the United States is what a flagpole might fly, so it is something a pole displays.

clue.text: Appeal for quiet colleges is binned, failing to start, unfortunately

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters are thrown into a new order
failing to start says the word loses its opening letter

explanation.surface: A plea for calm after colleges are scrapped, with the scheme sadly collapsing at the outset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'failing to start' trims binned to INNED; 'unfortunately' then rearranges COLLEGES IS INNED.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb is a plea for people to keep their mouths shut, praising the value of quietness.

clue.text: Aviatrix, very briefly flying, ordered for this transport?

indicators.note: ordered means arranged anew, so the remaining letters are rearranged
flying here means flying off, so that letter leaves the word

parts.note: V is the short form of very

explanation.surface: A female pilot is summoned to fly a charter plane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flying' takes V out of AVIATRIX, leaving AIATRIX; 'ordered' rearranges it. The whole clue also describes what an aviatrix might be booked for.
explanation.definitionFit: A small aircraft hired for short trips is a form of transport, as the question mark admits.

clue.text: Society anguish over plea for casual wear

indicators.note: in a down clue, over places the earlier pieces above the next one

parts.note: hell means torment or anguish
a suit is a plea or petition, as in a lawsuit

explanation.surface: Society suffers torment over a legal plea.
explanation.walkthrough: A shell suit is a shiny nylon tracksuit, popular in Britain in the late 1980s and early 1990s.
explanation.definitionFit: This lightweight tracksuit is leisure clothing, an example of informal dress.

clue.text: Pays attention to distinctive vocal sounds

definitions.meaning: to note something is to observe it or take heed of it
a singer produces musical tones, each one a separate pitch

explanation.surface: Someone listens closely to characteristic sounds of the voice.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means observes; as a plural noun it means musical tones sung by a voice.

clue.text: Fine example succeeded — the way with no violence reportedly

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for succeeded, as in family trees
how means the way or manner something is done

indicators.note: reportedly says the word is heard rather than seen, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: peace is the absence of violence

explanation.surface: A model case where success came through non-violent means.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reportedly' turns PEACE into its soundalike PIECE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something displayed as an outstanding specimen of its kind is a model item worth showing off.

clue.text: More prudent getting right to replace wide vertical pipe

indicators.note: to replace says one letter is swapped out for the other in the word

parts.note: wiser means more prudent
W is the cricket abbreviation for a wide

explanation.surface: A cautious person switches sides instead of going wide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting right to replace wide' swaps the W of WISER for R.
explanation.definitionFit: In plumbing and building, an upright pipe carrying water or gas between floors has this name.

clue.text: Restrict Margaret? Not happy

parts.note: Peg is a pet form of the name Margaret
down means low in spirits, unhappy

explanation.surface: Should Margaret be held back? She seems miserable.
explanation.definitionFit: To fix someone to a position or commitment is to limit their freedom, an idiom for constraint.

clue.text: Programme cost I'm breaking down — needs to be spelt out fully

definitions.text: Programme cost I'm breaking down — needs to be spelt out fully

parts.words: Programme cost I'm breaking down — needs to be spelt out fully
parts.note: rearranging COST IM gives the short form SITCOM, a television programme, which must then be written out in full

explanation.surface: A budget breakdown for a show has to be itemised in detail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking down' rearranges COST I'M into SITCOM; 'spelt out fully' asks for the unabbreviated term, so the grid takes the expanded form.
explanation.definitionFit: The full name of a sitcom is a television or radio programme built on recurring characters and humour.

clue.text: Somewhat stellar gesture, generous in the extreme

indicators.note: Somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A rather impressive act of kindness, generous to a fault.
explanation.definitionFit: Large can mean generous or liberal, so its superlative is the most generous possible.

clue.text: When observed, there's no turning back at location, I'd say

indicators.note: turning back says the word is read from right to left

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: I'd say signals speech, so a word that sounds the same is used

parts.note: a site is a location

explanation.surface: Someone at a spot declares there is no going back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning back' makes ON from NO; 'I'd say' turns SITE into SIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means as soon as something is seen, as in shoot on sight.

clue.text: Guy from Northern Ireland with everything?

parts.note: all means everything

explanation.surface: A question about a fellow from Ulster who has it all.
explanation.definitionFit: Guy here is a man's first name, and this Irish name is another example of one.

clue.text: Terribly nervous drinking quietly with a star

indicators.note: drinking means taking in, so one piece goes inside the other
terribly suggests disorder, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: A jittery celebrity has a quiet drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terribly' rearranges nervous to SUERNOV, and 'drinking' takes P in after its first two letters; 'star' looks like a celebrity but is the astronomical object.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an exploding star that suddenly becomes vastly brighter, so it is a kind of celestial body.

clue.text: Standards of behaviour quite possibly better after extremists leave

indicators.note: possibly suggests one of several arrangements, so the letters are reordered
the extremists are the outer letters, which depart from the word

explanation.surface: Rules of conduct might be improved once radicals depart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges QUITE into ETIQU; 'extremists leave' strips the B and R from better.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the code of polite conduct in society, the accepted rules of manners.

clue.text: Leader knocking trophy over, crazy when bottom's pinched?

indicators.note: over means knocked over, so the word is turned upside down in this down clue

parts.note: a pot is a slang term for a trophy or cup

indicators.note: the bottom, or last letter, is stolen from the word

parts.note: bananas is slang for crazy

explanation.surface: A captain topples the cup, going wild when someone's backside is nipped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' makes TOP from POT; 'bottom's pinched' removes the final S of BANANAS.
explanation.definitionFit: The informal phrase means the most important person in a group, the boss.

clue.text: By sound of it cricket side with small feeling of dissatisfaction

indicators.note: By sound of it means the words are heard, not spelt

parts.note: the on side is the half of a cricket field behind the batter's legs, and wee is Scottish for small: ON plus WEE

explanation.surface: A team that sounds puny leaves one discontented.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By sound of it' turns ON WEE into a soundalike: the French loanword is said roughly 'on-wee'.
explanation.definitionFit: This is listless weariness and boredom, a sense of discontent from lack of interest.

clue.text: Sentry and foe in struggle for command

indicators.note: in struggle suggests the letters are thrown about in a fight and come out reordered

explanation.surface: A guard and an enemy fight for control.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a military drill order telling soldiers to look straight ahead again.

clue.text: Initially sleeping poorly every night, they're exhausted

indicators.note: Initially says to take the opening letter of each following word

explanation.surface: People who sleep badly every night end up worn out.
explanation.definitionFit: Spent describes someone with no energy left, used up and tired out.

clue.text: Factor in running away to get married, having no work?

indicators.note: having no says these letters are taken out

parts.note: an elopement is running off secretly to marry
OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Is joblessness a reason for a couple to run off and wed?
explanation.definitionFit: An element is a component or contributing factor in a situation.

clue.text: SA openers trained in this period?

indicators.note: trained means drilled into shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: South Africa's opening batters practise during a certain time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trained' rearranges SA OPENERS; the whole clue also describes when cricket openers practise.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the stretch of time before a sports season starts, when teams train.

clue.text: Starving and ravenous, first of all eat fish?

indicators.note: first of all says to take the opening letter of each of those words

parts.note: dine means eat

explanation.surface: A famished, greedy person asks whether to have seafood.
explanation.definitionFit: The sardine is a small oily sea fish, an example of the category.

clue.text: Exaggerates importance of dramas completed earlier

indicators.note: earlier puts this piece in front of the other

parts.note: over means finished or completed
plays are dramas

explanation.surface: Plays that finished before are hyped beyond their worth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'earlier' sets the word for completed ahead of the word for dramas.
explanation.definitionFit: To overplay something is to make it seem more significant than it is, an idiom for overstating.

clue.text: Sauce from Dieppe store

indicators.note: from says the letters are taken out of the words that follow, spanning both

explanation.surface: A condiment bought from a shop in Dieppe, a French port.
explanation.definitionFit: Pesto is an Italian basil and pine-nut paste served on pasta, a kind of sauce.

clue.text: Sandbank crowd

definitions.meaning: a shallow bank of sand under the water is a hazard to boats
a large group of fish swimming together, or any throng

explanation.surface: A mass of people gathers on a sandbar.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a submerged sandbar and a large group of fish.

clue.text: Give up pro board game

parts.note: for means in favour of, pro
Go is a Japanese strategy board game

explanation.surface: A professional quits a game played on a board.
explanation.definitionFit: To forgo something is to do without it, to relinquish it.

clue.text: Hurry back by mid-year giving description of wet area

indicators.note: back says the word is read in reverse

parts.note: speed means hurry

indicators.note: mid says to take the middle letters of the word

explanation.surface: Rushing home by midsummer to describe a soggy region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns SPEED into DEEPS; 'mid' takes EA from year.
explanation.definitionFit: The ocean far from shore is the sea's deepest part, and this adjective describes it.

clue.text: Oddly Old Boy with pay increase gets perfume perhaps

indicators.note: Oddly says take the letters in the odd positions

parts.note: a rise is a pay increase in British usage

explanation.surface: A former pupil oddly gets a salary bump and some scent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly' takes the first, third and fifth letters of OLD BOY. An old boy is a former pupil of a British school.
explanation.definitionFit: To give something a smell is to scent it, and perfuming is one way of doing that.

clue.text: Six perfect balls in this game? Long odds against that!

definitions.text: Six perfect balls in this game? Long odds against that!

parts.words: Six perfect balls in this game? Long odds against that!
parts.note: in the UK state draw, winning the jackpot needs all six numbered balls drawn to match a ticket, which is very unlikely

explanation.surface: Six flawless deliveries in a cricket match would be a long shot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Six perfect balls' suggests a cricket over; it is six lottery balls drawn. The National Lottery is the UK's state-run lottery.
explanation.definitionFit: The UK draw is a game of chance where matching six balls brings the jackpot at very long odds.
